feeds_accelerator_ids.locator: SPS Operations group, "History", section "The LEP era"
feeds_accelerator_ids.note: Start = LEP's first beam, 14 July 1989 ("LEP was commissioned in July 1989 and the first beam circulated in the collider on 14 July.", CERN LEP page); earlier octant tests in 1988 are in the Warner paper. End = "LEP was closed down on 2 November 2000". The SPS received e+/e- from the PS at 3.5 GeV and delivered 20 GeV (the LEP injector linacs LIL and the accumulator EPA have no Atlas record).
feeds_accelerator_ids.quote: With the commissioning of the Large Electron-Positron Collider in July 1989, the SPS got a new role as an injector, sending electrons and positrons to LEP at an energy of 20 GeV.

feeds_accelerator_ids.locator: SPS Operations group, "History", section "LHC run 1 and 2"
feeds_accelerator_ids.note: Start = the first LHC beam, which came from the SPS. Injection energy 450 GeV (IPAC 2024: "SPS beams at 450 GeV are injected into the LHC via 2 transfer lines, TI2 and TI8").
feeds_accelerator_ids.quote: On 10 September 2008, the first beam from the SPS made a successful loop of the LHC.

feeds_accelerator_ids.locator: SPS Operations group, "History"; HiLumi LHC page
feeds_accelerator_ids.note: Derived and planned: the HL-LHC is the upgrade of the LHC ring (accelerator:lhc) and keeps its injector chain; CERN says the HiLumi LHC "should be operational in mid-2030". The quote documents the existing SPS to LHC link that the HL-LHC inherits.
feeds_accelerator_ids.quote: On 10 September 2008, the first beam from the SPS made a successful loop of the LHC.

intervals.label: operating
intervals.locator: end: home.cern, "All CERN accelerators now on the road to HiLumi", 31 August 2026
intervals.note: End = 31 August 2026, when "CERN’s injector complex and Antimatter Factory took their final steps towards Long Shutdown 3 (LS3) this morning, as the last particle beams were extracted and the machines fell silent." The 20 August 2026 accelerator report had scheduled the switch-off of all machines for 6.00 a.m. on Monday, 31 August.
intervals.quote: The SPS became the workhorse of CERN's particle physics programme when it switched on in 1976.

intervals.label: proton-antiproton collider (SppS)
intervals.note: Years taken from the operating period of UA1, which ran only during the Sp̄pS collider era; home.cern's SPS page dates the W and Z discovery to 1983 'with the SPS running as a proton-antiproton collider'.
intervals.quote: It ran from 1981 until 1990, when the SPS was used as a proton-antiproton collider

intervals.label: Long Shutdown 3 (injector complex)
intervals.note: Start = 31 August 2026 (CERN news item of that date). End is a schedule value: "Following the long shutdown, CERN’s accelerator complex will gradually come back to life, beginning with Linac4, the PS Booster and ISOLDE at the start of 2028." (20 August 2026) and "The complex will progressively return to operation from 2028 onwards, with the different injectors and facilities restarting in stages." (31 August 2026).
intervals.quote: CERN’s injector complex and Antimatter Factory took their final steps towards Long Shutdown 3 (LS3) this morning, as the last particle beams were extracted and the machines fell silent.

intervals.label: LEP injector (e+/e-)
intervals.note: The SPS accelerated electrons and positrons from 3.5 GeV to 20 GeV for LEP (the paper describes the design; the SPS history page confirms "an energy of 20 GeV" in the LEP era).
intervals.quote: Similarly the SPS operates as an e+/e- synchrotron between 3.5 GeV and 20 GeV, the nominal LEP injection energy.

injection_energy.quote: Similarly the SPS operates as an e+/e- synchrotron between 3.5 GeV and 20 GeV, the nominal LEP injection energy.

name: Super Proton Synchrotron
notes: CONFLICT on the Sp̄pS collider era: home.cern's UA1 page gives 1981-1990 ('It ran from 1981 until 1990, when the SPS was used as a proton-antiproton collider'); some literature extends the era to 1991. The sourced 1981-1990 is recorded.
is_collider is false because the SPS is normally a synchrotron injector; its proton-antiproton collider operation is carried as a separate interval.

The North Area fixed-target beams (beamline:cern-north-area) and the CNGS neutrino beam (beamline:cngs) were extracted from the SPS at 400 GeV/c; the SPS history page says the North Area "took beams of 400 and later 450 GeV".

beam_energy.quote: The SPS operates at up to 450 GeV.

circumference.quote: Measuring nearly 7 kilometres in circumference, it takes particles from the Proton Synchrotron and accelerates them to provide beams for the Large Hadron Collider...

injection_energy.note: Energy of the beam from the PS (26 GeV per CERN's accelerator-complex page; the LS2 media kit writes 25 GeV, see accelerator:ps). Beams for the LHC and the North Area leave the SPS at up to 450 GeV.
injection_energy.quote: These are accelerated to 2 GeV for injection into the Proton Synchrotron (PS), which pushes the beam up to 26 GeV. Protons are then sent to the Super Proton Synchrotron (SPS), where they are accelerated up to 450 GeV.

summary.plain: A seven-kilometre ring at CERN that has been the laboratory's workhorse since 1976. It accelerates protons to 450 billion electronvolts and hands them to the Large Hadron Collider, and in the 1980s it was rebuilt to collide protons with antiprotons, which is how the W and Z particles were discovered.
summary.technical: ~7 km proton synchrotron, 1317 room-temperature magnets, top energy 450 GeV; LHC injector and fixed-target source for the North Area, NA61/SHINE, NA62, COMPASS and AWAKE; operated as the Sp̄pS proton-antiproton collider for UA1/UA2 from 1981 to 1990.
